To cut a release, push a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`. CI then builds and publishes it. Don't publish by hand.

```sh
git checkout main && git pull
make test                      # optional sanity check before tagging
git tag v2026.10.1             # year.month.sequence; N is the Nth release that month
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

This comes from a project memory written by a human ("Release by tagging vYYYY.MM.N", for example `v2026.09.2`). The repo itself doesn't confirm it:

- **No CI config here.** There's no `.github/workflows` or similar, so I can't see what the tag triggers or check that it publishes. The pipeline probably lives somewhere else.
- **No tags in this clone.** That means I can't tell what number to use next. Run `git fetch --tags` and look at the latest `v2026.10.*` tag before you choose `N`. If there isn't one yet, this month's first release would be `v2026.10.1`.
- **No release docs.** The README and Makefile don't mention releases. The Makefile only has `test` and `test-fast`.

It would help to check with whoever owns the CI pipeline before your first release, and to add a short release section to the README.
